saml.description: When SAML username mapping is missing or empty, Casdoor derives the username from email first and falls back to NameID only if email is unavailable.
saml.note: Different upstream identifiers may intentionally map to the same downstream username if email linking/fallback is configured.

saml.description: Casdoor can automatically link external-provider logins to existing users by provider identity, email/phone if enabled, or case-insensitive username.
saml.note: Identity merges under configured linking policy are expected behavior, not necessarily a collision bug.

saml.description: Casdoor normalizes email addresses to lowercase for uniqueness.
saml.note: Case-only email differences should not be flagged as identity collisions.

saml.description: SAML providers always appear as buttons on the login page and require explicit user selection, even when SAML is the only configured provider.
saml.note: Lack of automatic redirect is by design and should not be treated as flow inconsistency.

saml.description: Valid bearer access tokens can be reused across multiple API calls until expiry.
saml.note: Do not flag ordinary bearer token reuse as replay unless the artifact is documented as one-time.

saml.description: Acceptance of tokens without nbf, or lack of nbf enforcement, is spec-compliant because nbf is optional.
saml.note: Do not report missing nbf enforcement alone as a vulnerability.

saml.description: Not-before claim enforcement is optional for JWT processing.
saml.note: Acceptance of tokens without nbf or with future nbf is not automatically a vulnerability.

saml.description: When an admin changes SAML/OAuth provider configuration or metadata, acceptance under the new trust anchor is expected.
saml.note: Admin-initiated trust changes are by design; only stale acceptance of old trust after intended replacement is suspicious.

saml.description: Old signing keys may remain accepted until JWKS cache expires after rotation.
saml.note: Do not flag old-key acceptance before cache expiry.

saml.description: Casdoor can be configured to sign only the SAML response envelope while disabling assertion signatures for compatibility with some service providers.
saml.note: Acceptance of response-only signatures may be intentional compatibility behavior.

saml.description: With exclusive sign-in enabled, a new login for the same user and application invalidates previous sessions.
saml.note: Subsequent failures on older sessions are by design, not replay protection evidence.

saml.description: Calling /api/sso-logout without logoutAll=false logs the user out from all sessions and expires all tokens.
saml.note: Global logout side effects should not be mistaken for inconsistent session handling.

saml.description: Application tag restrictions do not apply to admins and global admins.
saml.note: Admin access to a tagged application is by design and not an authorization escalation.

saml.constraint: For SAML upstream testing against Casdoor as SP, the Assertion Consumer Service endpoint is /api/acs and it accepts POST only. The IdP under test MUST use HTTP POST binding; redirect/GET binding to /api/acs will fail and is not a security signal.
saml.source: provider/saml/overview.md, provider/saml/custom.md, provider/saml/keycloak.md, provider/saml/google-workspace.md, provider/saml/azure-ad.md, provider/saml/aliyun.md

saml.constraint: Casdoor SAML username mapping has fallback semantics: if the username attribute is not explicitly mapped or is empty, Casdoor first uses the email attribute as username, and if email is absent it falls back to NameID. For I4 collision tests, the fuzzer MUST control email and NameID carefully and MUST NOT assume NameID is always the bound principal.

For SAML provider setup, Casdoor derives Endpoint, IdP, Issuer URL, SP ACS URL, and SP Entity ID by parsing uploaded metadata. The fuzzer MUST provide valid IdP metadata when creating a SAML provider; these trust-anchor fields are not independently documented as direct API inputs in the provided docs.

Casdoor supports account linking for external providers by OAuth identity, email/phone if enabled, or username case-insensitively. For cross-protocol I4 tests involving SAML, a same-email login may intentionally link to an existing account rather than create a distinct identity. The fuzzer MUST distinguish configured account linking from unintended identity collapse.

For I3 MFA-bypass-via-binding-rule tests, MFA is enforced as an application/user feature and alternate providers are attached to applications with rules. A valid test MUST first establish that password login for the same user/application triggers MFA, then compare SAML login through the same application. Do not compare across different applications or provider-rule configurations.

Application tag restrictions apply after authentication: only users with at least one matching tag may sign in, except admins/global admins who bypass tag restrictions. For I5 authorization-binding tests, do not use admin accounts as subjects because they are exempt and will create false positives.

Numeric sentinel: application Code resend timeout uses 0 as a sentinel meaning use the global default, not literal zero seconds. Never assume 0 disables waiting. Tests that depend on resend timing MUST set an explicit positive value or account for fallback to the global default.

Numeric sentinel: application CookieExpireInHours uses 0 as a sentinel meaning use the default cookie lifetime, not immediate expiry. Documentation states default is 720 hours, and without Remember me the session is limited to 24 hours. Never interpret 0 as zero-hour expiry in freshness tests.

For OAuth/OIDC tokens issued after SAML login, the resource parameter must match exactly between the authorization request and token request. Audience-binding tests using resource indicators MUST keep the same absolute URI in both steps or failures are setup errors rather than security behavior.

For token exchange scope-escalation tests, Casdoor documents that requested scope should be a subset of the original token scope and omitted scope inherits the subject token scope. The fuzzer MUST include a baseline subject token with known limited scope before attempting expansion, otherwise acceptance/rejection cannot be interpreted correctly.

For I2 expired-assertion or future/timing tests, include a control flow using a valid token/assertion first. Casdoor docs expose standard OAuth token issuance and SAML provider setup, but a failed attack login could also be caused by bad application/provider wiring. A control login is required to distinguish broken setup from correct freshness enforcement.

SSO logout supports logoutAll=true by default and logoutAll=false for current-session-only logout. Because logoutAll defaults to full logout when omitted, cleanup or session-lifecycle tests MUST set logoutAll explicitly to avoid unintentionally revoking all sessions and invalidating later sequence steps.
Casdoor SAML SP ACS endpoint is POST-only at /api/acs. The fuzzer MUST submit SAMLResponse via HTTP POST form binding; GET-based SAML callbacks will be rejected and are not valid tests.

For SAML login tests, the executor MUST initiate the SP flow first and preserve the resulting request context before posting to /api/acs. Casdoor documentation states the ACS consumes IdP POSTs and the SAML flow is SP-initiated; sending a fabricated unsolicited response without matching flow state can fail for non-security reasons.

Casdoor's SAML SP identity mapping has documented fallback semantics: if username mapping is absent or empty, Casdoor first uses email as username, then falls back to NameID. For I4 multi-identity tests, the fuzzer MUST control both email and NameID and must not assume NameID is always the bound principal.

For I4 SAML email-binding collision tests, Casdoor may derive the username from email before NameID. To test whether distinct upstream principals collapse, send attacker-controlled NameID with victim email and verify the resulting Casdoor account identity via /api/userinfo and /api/get-account rather than assuming NameID is authoritative.

Casdoor supports automatic account linking by email/phone or case-insensitive username for external providers. For SAML identity-collision tests, pre-existing local users with matching email or username can be linked by design. The fuzzer MUST distinguish intended linking behavior from unintended principal collapse and should vary email/username independently.

SAML assertion signature behavior is configurable per application. Casdoor can disable assertion-level signatures while still signing only the response envelope. For I1 tests such as saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_spurious_signature, and saml_post_binding_unsigned_assertion, the fuzzer MUST record whether Enable SAML assertion signature is enabled; acceptance of response-only signatures may be a compatibility configuration choice rather than proof that signature checks are skipped universally.

Casdoor documentation states SAML responses are always signed, but assertion signatures can be disabled for compatibility. For I1 proof-integrity tests, do not treat acceptance of an unsigned assertion as a vulnerability unless the application is configured to expect assertion signatures or the platform accepts attacker-controlled signatures/trust anchors.

Issuer and endpoint values for SAML providers are derived from uploaded metadata via Parse. For I1 issuer-mismatch and trust-anchor tests, the fuzzer MUST create providers with explicit metadata and verify the parsed issuer/endpoint fields correspond to the intended IdP. A malformed or mismatched metadata upload can invalidate the setup rather than demonstrate missing issuer validation.

Casdoor's /api/userinfo response is scope-dependent. For verification after SAML login, the fuzzer MUST request sufficient scopes (at least openid, and profile/email when needed) or use /api/get-account as a secondary verifier. Missing fields in /api/userinfo can otherwise look like identity loss or authorization failure.

When testing I5 audience/resource binding on tokens obtained after SAML-backed login, if the authorization request uses RFC 8707 resource, the token request MUST repeat the exact same resource value. Casdoor documents exact matching between authorize and token requests; mismatch causes setup failure unrelated to audience enforcement.

Numeric sentinel: application Code resend timeout uses 0 as a sentinel meaning 'use the global default', not literal zero seconds. Never assume 0 disables waiting. Tests that depend on immediate resend behavior MUST set an explicit positive value instead of 0.

Numeric sentinel: application CookieExpireInHours uses 0 as a sentinel meaning 'use default' rather than zero lifetime. Documentation states default is 720h and non-remembered sessions are limited to 24h. Do not use 0 to create instantly expired sessions in freshness tests.

Numeric sentinel: inactiveTimeoutMinutes empty or <=0 means no timeout. Do not interpret 0 as immediate expiry; it disables inactivity timeout. Freshness tests must use explicit positive inactivity values if they rely on timeout behavior.

Refresh token expiration default is 0 hours at the application level. The fuzzer MUST treat 0 as a special configuration value from the application settings, not assume a usable refresh lifetime. If refresh or long-lived session behavior is under test, set RefreshExpireInHours explicitly to a positive value.

Casdoor supports exclusive sign-in: a new login deletes all previous sessions for that user and application. For I3 flow-coherence and multi-session tests, the fuzzer MUST disable EnableExclusiveSignin unless the test specifically targets single-session behavior, or later logins will invalidate earlier sessions by design.

Session-use budget analysis: exclusive sign-in and SSO logout operate on sessions globally. Any verification call made after a second login may fail because the first session was intentionally removed. The fuzzer MUST not interpret 401/403 after a second login as replay protection unless exclusive sign-in is disabled.

Casdoor supports full SSO logout by default on /api/sso-logout when logoutAll is omitted or true. Cleanup or session-management steps MUST set logoutAll=false if the test needs other active sessions to remain valid; otherwise all sessions and tokens for the user are invalidated by design.

For I2 expired-assertion and other freshness tests, include a control login with a valid SAML assertion first. Casdoor SAML setup depends on provider attachment, application routing, and ACS POST binding; without a control, a failed attack login cannot be distinguished from broken SAML configuration.

For I3 MFA-bypass-via-binding-rule tests, MFA must be enabled on the target user before comparing password and SAML paths. Casdoor supports multiple MFA methods and preferred MFA selection; a valid test must first confirm password login triggers MFA challenge for that same user/application.

Casdoor applications can enable account linking via email and external-provider linking. For unverified-email-account-linking tests, the fuzzer MUST verify whether linking-by-email is enabled and whether the SAML provider/application is attached to the target app; otherwise observed merges may be configured behavior rather than a vulnerability.

Application tags restrict sign-in to users whose tags intersect the application's tags, except admins/global admins. For I5 authorization tests, the fuzzer MUST either align user tags with application tags or leave application tags unset. A denied login due to tag mismatch is not evidence of SAML assertion rejection.

Shared applications rewrite client identifiers with the suffix -org-<organization>. For cross-org or cross-tenant token/audience tests, the fuzzer MUST use the organization-specific client_id form when the application is shared; otherwise audience and redirect mismatches can invalidate the test setup.

Casdoor normalizes email addresses to lowercase. For I4 case-confusion tests involving email-derived usernames from SAML assertions, the fuzzer MUST expect lowercase normalization and should use non-email NameID variants to test case sensitivity independently.

If organization setting isUsernameLowered is enabled, usernames are converted to lowercase. For I4 case-confusion tests, the fuzzer MUST check this setting because Admin vs admin may collapse by configuration rather than by a SAML-specific bug.

Casdoor's /api/userinfo can be called either with Bearer token or accessToken query parameter. Verification sequences should use one method consistently; mixing methods is unnecessary and can complicate CORS or client behavior analysis.
Casdoor SAML ACS is POST-only at /api/acs. The fuzzer MUST submit SAMLResponse via HTTP POST form encoding; GET-based SAML callback tests will fail for transport reasons, not security reasons.

Casdoor username mapping for SAML has fallback semantics: if the IdP does not provide an explicit username mapping or it is empty, Casdoor first uses the email attribute as username, and if no email is available it falls back to NameID. I4 tests MUST control both email and NameID because identity binding may occur on email before NameID.

Casdoor supports automatic account linking for external providers by OAuth identity, email/phone if enabled, or username case-insensitively. For cross-user collision and account-linking tests, the fuzzer MUST distinguish intended linking behavior from identity confusion and should disable or avoid email-based linking when testing SAML identity uniqueness.

For SAML issuer-validation tests, create_provider SHOULD include parsed metadata so issuerUrl and IdP are populated. If metadata/issuer configuration is absent or incomplete, issuer trust may be under-specified and an accepted assertion may reflect incomplete setup rather than an I1 failure.

Casdoor as SAML IdP can disable assertion-level signatures while still signing the response envelope via application setting EnableSamlAssertionSignature=false. When testing assertion-level integrity issues such as unsigned assertion or envelope-only signature acceptance, the fuzzer MUST account for this documented compatibility mode and verify whether the SP under test is accepting envelope-only signatures by design from Casdoor configuration.

For SAML POST-vs-GET binding tests against Casdoor as IdP, Reply URL controls binding: if Reply URL is filled, Casdoor sends SAMLResponse by POST; if empty, Casdoor uses GET and derives ACS from the SAMLRequest. Tests that assume POST binding MUST configure SAML reply URL explicitly.

Application tag enforcement restricts sign-in to users whose tags intersect the application's tags, but admins and global admins are exempt. Authorization-binding tests using admin accounts will produce false positives because admins bypass tag restrictions by design.

Exclusive sign-in deletes prior sessions on each new sign-in for the same user and application. Replay/coherence tests that rely on multiple concurrent sessions for one principal MUST disable EnableExclusiveSignin or use separate applications/users, otherwise earlier sessions are invalidated by design.

Numeric sentinel: application CodeResendTimeout uses 0 as a sentinel meaning use the global default, not literal zero seconds. Never assume 0 disables waiting; set a positive explicit value when timing behavior matters.

Numeric sentinel: application CookieExpireInHours uses 0 to mean use the default cookie lifetime, not immediate expiry. Documentation states default is 720 hours, and without Remember me the session is limited to 24 hours. Do not use 0 in freshness tests expecting zero lifetime.

Numeric sentinel: application RefreshExpireInHours defaults to 0 hours unless explicitly set on the application. Tests involving refresh tokens or long-lived sessions MUST set a nonzero refresh lifetime explicitly; otherwise refresh behavior may fail due to configuration, not security enforcement.

For audience-binding tests using RFC 8707 resource indicators, the resource parameter must match exactly between /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token. A mismatch changes token issuance semantics and can cause false positives in I5 audience tests.

For I2 token-freshness tests against Casdoor OAuth/OIDC tokens, include a control login using a valid token flow before attack variants. Otherwise a failed exchange or userinfo call may reflect broken application/provider setup rather than freshness enforcement.

Casdoor shared applications use organization-specific client identifiers by appending -org-<organizationName> to the client_id or application name. Cross-organization audience or tenant-isolation tests MUST use the org-suffixed client_id where shared applications are enabled, or results will be misattributed.

Casdoor normalizes email addresses to lowercase for uniqueness. Tests that compare identities by email must treat case-only differences as equivalent and should not flag lowercase normalization as an I4 collision.

If organization setting isUsernameLowered is enabled, usernames are converted to lowercase. Case-confusion tests MUST first determine whether this normalization is configured; otherwise Admin vs admin collapsing may be by configuration, not a vulnerability.

Casdoor SAML providers always appear as buttons on the login page and do not auto-redirect even when they are the sole provider. Flow-coherence tests MUST model an explicit provider selection step before expecting SAML redirection.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: A pre-configured test environment exists: organization 'test-org', application 'app-test' (query clientId/clientSecret via GET /api/get-application?id=admin/app-test), and SAML provider 'provider-saml-test' already linked to app-test. For MOST tests, REUSE these resources instead of creating new ones. Only create new organizations/applications when the attack specifically requires distinct tenants (e.g., I5 cross-org token exchange). OWNERSHIP RULES: Applications and providers MUST use owner='admin'. Users MUST use owner=<organization_name> (e.g., 'test-org'). NEVER use 'built-in' as organization for create_user — the built-in org forbids user creation. GRANT TYPES: When creating applications, ALWAYS include grantTypes=['password','authorization_code','urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange'] and enablePassword=true and cert='cert-built-in' unless the test specifically requires otherwise. MULTI-APP SEQUENCES: When a test needs two separate applications (e.g., token exchange between different clients/audiences), use 'app-test' as the SOURCE application (already exists) and create ONE new application as the TARGET. Create users with signupApplication matching the app they will login to. For login_with_password, the executor auto-resolves client_id from the user's signupApplication — so set signupApplication correctly in create_user.
